claim: For any linearly independent triple \(S=\{\lvert\psi_1\rangle,\lvert\psi_2\rangle,\lvert\psi_3\rangle\}\subset\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2\), fix \(k\) and identify two-qubit vectors with \(2\times2\) coefficient matrices. Let \(W_k=\operatorname{span}\{\psi_j:j\ne k\}^{\perp}\), choose nonzero \(C_k\) spanning \(W_k\cap\psi_k^{\perp}\), and choose any \(D_k\in W_k\setminus\mathbb C C_k\). Then \(\lvert\psi_k\rangle\) has no LOCC-unambiguous product detector if and only if \(\det C_k=0\), \(\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{adj}(C_k)D_k)=0\), and \(\det D_k\ne0\). Equivalently, the projective line \(\mathbb P(W_k)\) is tangent to the Segre product-state quadric at the unique point \(\mathbb P(W_k\cap\psi_k^{\perp})\). Consequently the whole triple is locally unambiguously discriminable exactly when this tangency obstruction is absent for all three indices.

correctness.rationale: For each index, Chefles reduces LOCC-unambiguous identifiability to a product vector in a two-dimensional orthogonal-complement plane outside one state-orthogonal line. Under the two-qubit matrix identification the product condition is det=0, so restricting determinant to the plane gives a homogeneous quadratic. Absence of a detector is exactly a single double projective root at the state-orthogonal point, equivalent to det(C)=0, tr(adj(C)D)=0, det(D) nonzero. The known Bell obstruction and a 1000-triple regression check agree with the analytic criterion.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial exceptional case in the dimension-threshold theorem receives a complete and directly computable classification. The criterion distinguishes transverse two-product intersections, lines contained in the product quadric, and the unique tangent failure, giving both an operational test and a geometric explanation rather than an arbitrary finite example.
